title: Given K sorted arrays, merge them into a single sorted array. Explain the K-way Merge technique with a heap, the complexity, and a banking use case.
shortTitle: Merge K Sorted Arrays (Combine K Sorted Arrays into One Sorted Array)

s1_definition.profdef: Merge K Sorted Arrays is the array form of the K-way Merge pattern. We keep a min-heap of one candidate per array, each entry remembering the array index and position, pop the global minimum into the output, and push the successor from the same array. With N total elements across K arrays the merge runs in N log K time and K space.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India has K sorted arrays of daily settlement amounts, one per desk. To build one chronological settlement sheet, a clerk keeps the earliest unused amount from each desk, writes the smallest, and pulls the next amount from that same desk. The desk tray never holds more than K slips.
s1_definition.oneliner: Same engine as merging K lists, but over arrays with index-and-position heap entries.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Merge K Sorted Arrays is the array form of the K-way Merge pattern. We keep a min-heap of one candidate per array, each entry remembering the array index and position, pop the global minimum into the output, and push the successor from the same array. With N total elements across K arrays the merge runs in N log K time and K space.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** The National Bank of India has K sorted arrays of daily settlement amounts, one per desk. To build one chronological settlement sheet, a clerk keeps the earliest unused amount from each desk, writes the smallest, and pulls the next amount from that same desk. The desk tray never holds more than K slips.

**One line to remember:** Same engine as merging K lists, but over arrays with index-and-position heap entries.

sections.s2_technical:
With arrays we cannot follow a `next` pointer, so each heap entry carries the value, the array index, and the element index: `{value, arrayIndex, elementIndex}`. We seed the heap with the first element of each non-empty array, then pop repeatedly. On each pop we append the value to the result and, if the element index plus one is still within that array, push the next element.

A concrete seed looks like `pq.add(new int[]{arrays[i][0], i, 0})`. On pop of `{v, ai, ei}` we do `result.add(v)` and, if `ei + 1 < arrays[ai].length`, `pq.add(new int[]{arrays[ai][ei+1], ai, ei+1})`. Senior nuance: pre-sizing the output to the known total avoids repeated growth, and because each element is pushed and popped exactly once the comparisons total N log K, strictly better than N log N re-sorting when K is small relative to N.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — The National Bank of India collects daily settlement amounts from K processing desks, each desk's array already sorted. The operations team needs one combined sorted array for the end-of-day reconciliation, and re-sorting the combined pile wastes the existing order. This is exactly how Merge K Sorted Arrays works: it merges in N log K by reusing each array's order.

The code defines a `SettlementSheetService` exposing `mergeKArrays(arrays)` returning one sorted array. A `Demo` builds three sorted arrays and logs the merged sheet.

sections.s5_journey:
The input is three sorted arrays: desk one 5, 12, 19; desk two 3, 8, 20; desk three 1, 14. The known total is eight elements.

Step 1 — We seed the heap with the first elements 5, 3, and 1, each tagged with array index and position zero. The output array of size eight is allocated and empty.

Step 2 — Pop 1 from desk three, place it at output position zero, push desk three's next, 14. Heap holds 5, 3, 14.

Step 3 — Pop 3 from desk two, place at position one, push 8. Heap holds 5, 8, 14.

Step 4 — Pop 5 from desk one, place at position two, push 12. Heap holds 12, 8, 14. We continue: 8 then push 20, 12 then push 19, 14 (desk three ends), 19, 20.

Step 5 — The heap empties and the output array is fully sorted. The merged sheet is shown below.

```
Oct 27, 2026 8:46:40 PM com.bank.sheet.service.SettlementSheetService mergeKArrays
INFO: Merged 3 arrays, 8 elements
Oct 27, 2026 8:46:40 PM com.bank.sheet.SettlementSheetApplication main
INFO: Merged settlement sheet: [1, 3, 5, 8, 12, 14, 19, 20]
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Merge K Sorted Arrays is the array form of the K-way Merge pattern. Because arrays have no next pointer, each heap entry carries the value together with the array index and the element index, so after I pop a value I can fetch its successor in the same array. I seed the min-heap with the first element of every array, then pop the global minimum into the output and push the next element from whichever array I just drew from.

The efficiency argument is the same as for lists. The heap holds at most K candidates, one per array, so each of the N total elements is pushed and popped once at log K cost, giving N log K overall rather than the N log N of collecting everything and re-sorting. I usually pre-size the output array to the known total so there is no repeated resizing, which matters when the combined set is large.

At the National Bank of India I used this to build one end-of-day settlement sheet from several processing desks, each of which already produced its amounts in sorted order. I kept one earliest amount per desk in a heap and drained them into a single sorted array for reconciliation. Explaining that the heap entry must carry array and element indices, that the heap stays bounded by K, and that this beats re-sorting when K is small is what shows an interviewer that I apply the K-way Merge pattern correctly to arrays.
